html:
An outbreak of bubonic plague in British Hong Kong in 1894, part of the third plague pandemic. It was here that the plague germ was first identified, and from this port the disease spread by ship around the world.

The pandemic began in Yunnan in southwest China in the 1850s and moved slowly east. In 1894 it hit Canton and then Hong Kong, killing a few thousand people, most of them poor Chinese in crowded housing. The colonial government searched homes, burned property and isolated the sick, which caused anger and many Chinese fled to the mainland.

Two scientists raced to find the cause. The Japanese Kitasato Shibasaburō and the Swiss-French Alexandre Yersin of the Pasteur Institute both worked there in June 1894. Yersin clearly described the bacillus, later named Yersinia pestis after him. A few years later others showed that rat fleas spread it.

Steamships carried plague from Hong Kong to ports across the world. It reached Bombay in 1896, and India suffered most, with millions of deaths. It is the same disease as the Black Death.
sum: An outbreak of bubonic plague in British Hong Kong in 1894, part of the third plague pandemic. It was here that the plague germ was first identified, and from this port the disease spread by ship around the world.
